title: Evidence of First Peoples in Australia
summary: Archaeological evidence places First Peoples in Australia at least 65,000 years ago. This establishes a deep history of human life on the continent.

citations.locator: Evidence of first peoples; ochre image caption
citations.note: Supports the factual summary and chronology. Context includes explicitly interpretive comparisons; the date note identifies limits of precision.

claims.text: Archaeological evidence places First Peoples in Australia at least 65,000 years ago. This establishes a deep history of human life on the continent.
At least 65,000 years ago; 63,000 BCE is only a rounded placement and the earlier extent remains unknown.
An earliest surviving trace sets a minimum antiquity, not an exact arrival date. Living Aboriginal histories and knowledge should not be reduced to a single archaeological milestone.
